geo.title: Country-targeted pull
geo.diNote: Each DataImpulse product has its own login and password, so the product is chosen by the credentials you enter above. Pick the matching name here and the pulled proxies are labelled with it, which keeps several products apart in the pool.
geo.anyipApiNote: Two ways to connect: paste your proxy Username + Password below (AnyIP dashboard: open a proxy profile and scroll to its proxy details), OR enter an API key + Team ID here to auto-provision a proxy account. The API key is NOT the proxy password.
geo.integrationTokenPlaceholder: Integration token from the API for developers page
geo.diStickyHelp: One proxy per profile. Each one keeps its own exit IP for the time you pick below.
geo.diRotatingHelp: One shared endpoint whose exit IP changes on every request. It adds a single proxy, so it suits scraping rather than logged-in profiles.
geo.diLookupHint: Loading shows how many live IPs each state or city has, as suggestions in the fields above. Separate several values with commas.
geo.diNeedCreds: Enter the plan login and password first.
geo.diCountTitle: Sticky proxies to add, up to 1000 per pull. One login has 10,001 sticky ports (10000 to 20000).
geo.howManyListTitle: How many of the proxies on your account to import. Leave blank for all.
geo.gatewayHintGeneric: Pre-filled with the {{provider}} default gateway ({{gateway}}). Change it only if your {{provider}} dashboard gives you a different host or port.
geo.gatewayHintNone: Paste the gateway host shown in your {{provider}} dashboard; the port is filled in for you when it is standard.
geo.howManyCapTitle: How many proxies to add; blank adds {{n}}. Most gateways allow up to 1000 per pull.
geo.sessionDigitsError: A sticky session is digits only, 1 to {{max}} of them, as in the provider's dashboard.

rotating.tip: Tip: a rotating gateway uses the same host:port for every session - your username/password (or sticky-session token) selects the exit IP.

apiSync.title: API Sync
apiSync.brightDataHelp: Zone IPs: pulls the zone's dedicated IPs through {{provider}}'s API and pins each one to the super-proxy gateway with the username and password above.
apiSync.verifyAfter: above against the {{provider}} gateway with a live request on the first proxy, then adds them all.
apiSync.ipv6Help: Appends -ipversion-6 to the username. If the target site publishes no AAAA record, Oxylabs falls back to IPv4 automatically, so an IPv6 pull does not guarantee an IPv6 exit. May need enabling on your Oxylabs account first.
apiSync.modeZoneHelp: Adds every dedicated IP of the zone, at most 5000, each pinned to its own IP. Needs the API token. A residential zone has no IPs to list, so use Sticky sessions for it.
apiSync.modeStickyHelp: Each proxy gets its own session, so each keeps its own exit IP. Up to 1000 per pull.
apiSync.modeRotatingHelp: Adds one endpoint whose exit IP changes on every request. It suits scraping rather than logged-in profiles.
apiSync.countTitle: How many sticky sessions to add, 1 to 1000.
apiSync.geoHint: State covers US states only. A city needs a country, and when both a city and a state are filled in, the city is used.
apiSync.geoHintCode: State covers US states only, as the two-letter code (for example NY for New York). A city needs a country, and when both a city and a state are filled in, the city is used.

result.noChangeIpLink_one: {{count}} phone has no change-IP link, so its proxies were added without Rotate IP. Create one in the iProxy dashboard and pull again to use Rotate IP.
result.noChangeIpLink_other: {{count}} phones have no change-IP link, so their proxies were added without Rotate IP. Create one in the iProxy dashboard and pull again to use Rotate IP.

errors.enterProviderToken: Enter your provider token to sync.
errors.enterUsernameFirst: Enter the proxy username above first.
errors.lookup: Could not reach the provider account.
errors.anyipCredsOrApi: Enter your proxy Username + Password, or an API key + Team ID to auto-provision.
errors.marsSubuserNotFound: MarsProxies found no sub-user with that username and password. Check them under Sub-users in the dashboard, and enter only the part of the password before the first underscore.

geoHints.apify: Apify residential routes through one gateway (proxy.apify.com:8000); the country, a US state code (for example CA) and a sticky session are encoded into the username. Residential proxies need a paid Apify plan. Each pull mints up to 1000 sticky residential IPs you can assign to profiles; Apify keeps each one for about 30 minutes. Use the password from Apify Console → Proxy → HTTP settings.
geoHints.anyip: anyip.io routes through one gateway (portal.anyip.io:1080, HTTP and SOCKS5) and encodes the pool type (Residential/Mobile), country, state and city, a sticky-session name and lifetime into the proxy username. A city needs its state, and a state needs a country. Connect either by pasting your proxy Username (user_…) + Password from the dashboard, OR by entering an API key + Team ID: the first such pull creates one proxy user on your AnyIP account, and later pulls on this computer with the same key and Team ID reuse it, because AnyIP limits proxy users per plan and cannot delete them. Each pull mints up to 1000 proxies, each with its own session. How many 1 with no session name and Keep same IP blank gives one rotating proxy (a new IP on every request); otherwise each proxy keeps its IP for the Keep same IP time, or AnyIP's default of 7 days when that is blank. A fixed session name pins one IP. Override the gateway if your dashboard shows a custom port.
geoHints.dataimpulse: Every pull adds new proxies. Sticky proxies sit on their own ports, so asking for 5 when the pool already holds 5 with the same settings adds the next 5 ports instead of returning the same ones. A pull adds up to 1000, and one login has 10,001 sticky ports in all. Use the login and password of one DataImpulse product, shown on that product page in the dashboard.
geoHints.proxyseller: Residential is a traffic package: each New list pull creates a list on your account named SoftGlaze plus the location and time, with up to 1000 ports (the most the API allows in one list), and each port is its own exit IP. For more, pull again to create another list. Entry server picks the server the proxies connect through. IPv6, IPv4, ISP, Mobile, IPv4 Mix and ISP Mix are sold per IP: the pull reads your orders page by page and adds every active IP you already own (at most 5000), each on its own port, and needs nothing created.
geoHints.iproyal: IPRoyal builds each proxy for you: the location and a sticky session go into the password, on its gateway geo.iproyal.com. Sticky proxies share one host and port, and each keeps its own exit IP for the lifetime you pick. A sticky pull adds up to 1000. Traffic comes out of your residential balance or the chosen sub-user.
geoHints.packetstream: PacketStream routes through one gateway, proxy.packetstream.io: HTTPS on 31111 (TLS to the proxy, the one PacketStream recommends), HTTP on 31112 and SOCKS5 on 31113. Enter the Username and the auth key from the dashboard's Proxy Access page (the auth key is not your account password). Pick a country to target it, or leave it on any; the list matches the Location list in the PacketStream dashboard. With How many at 1 and no session you get one proxy with a fresh rotating IP; above 1, or with a session name, you get that many sticky exit IPs (up to 1000, one per profile). A sticky IP holds while it gets a new connection at least once an hour, and fails rather than moving if its device goes offline. Traffic comes out of your PacketStream balance.
geoHints.airproxy: Airproxy sells dedicated mobile proxies (each its own SIM), all in Italy, so the app lists what is already on your account and marks each one IT. Paste your API key (dashboard, API section) and pull. How many caps the import (blank = all). The country is fixed by the SIM, so there is nothing to target. Protocol is HTTP unless you pick SOCKS5, which uses the same port (seen in the Airproxy dashboard, not stated in its docs); if SOCKS5 proxies fail the check, pull them again as HTTP. Rotate the IP from the Airproxy dashboard.
geoHints.catproxies: CatProxies uses your API key (My Account → API Keys, starts with cp_) plus the Plan ID of one plan from Active Plans. Pick the pool that matches that plan: Standard Residential, Premium Residential or Rotating Mobile. Choose a country, or leave it Worldwide; Residential also takes a state and a city (Premium: a US state or a city, not both), Mobile a region and a city. Gateway picks the US, Europe or Asia server; use the one nearest your target country. How many above 1, or a Keep same IP time, mints sticky IPs, up to 1000 (Keep same IP sets how long each holds, 30 minutes if blank: up to 24 hours on Standard, 7 days on Premium, 4 hours on Mobile); type a session name to choose their names. Residential is HTTP or SOCKS5; mobile is HTTP only. Traffic comes out of that plan's bandwidth. Dedicated or Custom ISP and Datacenter plans have fixed IPs, so the app imports the plan's IPs instead of minting them: State, City, Sticky session and Keep same IP do not apply there and are hidden, and so is Country on ISP (on Datacenter it filters the IPs). Leave How many blank to import every IP; a number caps the import.
geoHints.rapidproxy: RapidProxy has no management API, so the app builds the proxies on its gateway (us.rapidproxy.io:5001, HTTP and SOCKS5 on the same port; pick one under Protocol). Enter a sub-account username and password from the dashboard (Residential, sub-accounts; give it a traffic cap above 0). Pick a country or leave it on any; State and City are optional, and City needs a State. With How many at 1, no session and Keep same IP blank you get one proxy with a new IP on every request; above 1, with a session name or with a Keep same IP time, you get that many sticky IPs (up to 1000), and Keep same IP sets how long each holds (up to 3 hours; RapidProxy's own default if blank). Change the gateway host if your dashboard shows another server.
geoHints.novada: NOVADA builds each proxy on its gateway (super.novada.pro:7777, HTTP). Enter a proxy user created under Users, Add User (your login email does not work) and its password. Pick Residential, Rotating ISP or Mobile to match your plan, then a country; State and City are optional. How many 1 with no session name and Keep same IP blank gives one rotating proxy (a new IP on every request); more than 1, a session name or a Keep same IP time mints that many sticky IPs, up to 1000 per pull (the same limit as the dashboard endpoint generator). Keep same IP sets how long each holds (up to 120 minutes, or 360 on Rotating ISP; 10 if blank). Hosts are per account: if the dashboard endpoint generator shows another host, enter it as the gateway.
geoHints.proxiessx: Proxies.sx uses your API key (it needs the account:read scope) to read your gateway login and proxy password, then builds proxies on gw.proxies.sx (HTTP port 7000, SOCKS5 port 7001). Pick Mobile or Residential and a country; a country is required, and if it has no stock the pull stops instead of exiting from another country. Mobile runs only in the US, GB, FR, NL, PL and GE (Georgia); Residential covers many more countries and uses residential devices only. On Residential you can add a State as its 2-letter code (for example CA) and a City. How many 1 with no session name and Keep same IP blank gives one rotating proxy (a new endpoint on each connection); more than 1, a session name or a Keep same IP time mints that many sticky IPs, up to 250 per pull, the most sessions Proxies.sx runs at once on one account. Keep same IP sets how long Proxies.sx keeps each session (24 hours if blank); the IP can still change if its device goes offline. A new account allows only a few parallel connections (5 on the Starter tier, more as you buy more traffic, per its pricing page), and each open profile uses several, so many sticky proxies in use at once can hit that limit. To rotate a sticky IP, pull again with a new session name. Set a proxy password in the Proxies.sx dashboard first.
geoHints.mobileproxyspace: MobileProxy.Space sells dedicated mobile proxies, so the app lists what is already on your account. Paste your API token from the personal account and choose HTTP or SOCKS5 under Protocol. How many caps the import (blank = all). The country is fixed by each proxy, so there is nothing to target; each proxy comes in with its country and, where it has one, its equipment-independent address, which keeps working when MobileProxy.Space swaps the device behind it. Change the IP with the proxy's change-IP link in the MobileProxy.Space dashboard. Their API allows one identical request every few seconds, so wait a moment between pulls.
geoHints.proxysolutions: Proxy-Solutions lists the proxies already on your account. Paste the Integration token from the dashboard, API for developers page (the third box, not the API key above it) and choose HTTP or SOCKS5 under Protocol. Pick a country to import only the proxies in that country, and use How many to cap the import (blank = all). Expired proxies are skipped, and each proxy keeps the country and name it has in your account.
geoHints.proxmint: Proxmint uses a read-only API key (Settings, API keys, starts with pmk_). The app reads your product's gateway and login from it, so nothing else is needed. Pick the product you bought, a country (leave Any for worldwide) and optionally a state or a city; when both are set the city is used. How many above 1, or a Keep same IP time, mints sticky IPs, each held for the Keep same IP time (1 to 120 minutes, 30 if blank); type a session name to choose their names. HTTP uses port 823, SOCKS5 port 824. The key cannot buy anything or change settings.
geoHints.databay: Databay uses a proxy user, not your login email: dashboard, Proxy Users, copy the username and its password. Everything runs on gw.databay.co:8888, which carries HTTP and SOCKS5 on the same port. Pick Residential, Residential Flex, Mobile or Datacenter to match your plan, then a country. State and City show on Residential only, the one pool that takes them; the most specific one is used, and a city is matched without its country, so a name found in several countries (Paris, Springfield) can exit in another one. How many above 1, or a Keep same IP time, mints sticky IPs, up to 1000 per pull, each held for the Keep same IP time (30 minutes if blank): up to 120 minutes, or 30 on Residential Flex.
geoHints.proxy6: PROXY6 lists the active proxies on your account (IPv4, shared IPv4 and IPv6). Paste the API key from your account and choose HTTP or SOCKS5; a proxy set to only the other protocol is left out. Pick a country to import only the proxies in that country, and use How many to cap the import (blank = all). MTProto proxies are not imported. If your key has an IP restriction, this computer's IP must be on it.
geoHints.proxybonanza: Proxy Bonanza lists the proxies on your active plans. Paste the full API key from the user panel (Account settings, API Key); it ends with an exclamation mark and your user id. Choose HTTP or SOCKS5. Pick a country to import only the proxies in that country, and use How many to cap the import (blank = all). Each proxy uses its plan's login and password; an IP that comes without one (a plan set to IP authorization only) is not imported, so turn on login and password authentication for that plan to pull it.
geoHints.gsocks: Gsocks lists the proxies already on your account. Paste the API key from your dashboard and pick Residential or Mobile. How many caps the import (blank = all). Country, city and rotation are set when the proxy list is created in the Gsocks panel, so there is nothing to target here. Private and datacenter proxies are not imported, because Gsocks publishes no list format for them. Choose HTTP or SOCKS5 under Protocol; Gsocks serves both on each proxy's host and port.
geoHints.singaporemobileproxy: Singapore Mobile Proxy sells dedicated mobile proxies: each one is a single modem with its own data allowance (for example 200 GB), so a pull adds the proxies already on your account, one per modem. Paste the client API key (reseller keys do not work) and choose HTTP or SOCKS5; leave How many blank to add them all. Each proxy keeps its rotation link, so Rotate IP in the proxy pool, and switching on a block page, give it a new mobile IP (at most every few minutes). Every proxy is in Singapore (the vendor sells no other country) and comes in marked SG; its data allowance is set by the plan, and more proxies are bought on the vendor's site. Only active proxies with a username and password are added.
geoHints.node4: Node4 uses an API key that starts with n4k_ (Account Settings, API & Webhooks); give it the read:proxies permission only. Pick the product: Residential, Rotating Datacenter or Rotating Unmetered build logins on Node4's gateways, and Static Datacenter imports the dedicated or shared IPs you already have. On Residential you can add a state, a city and an ASN. How many 1 adds one rotating login with a new exit for each connection; more adds that many sticky logins, up to 1000 per pull, each holding its exit for up to 30 minutes. HTTP or SOCKS5. The free tier is HTTP only.
geoHints.proxyempire: ProxyEmpire uses an API token from the panel (Settings, API Tokens); give it no more abilities than the pull needs. Pick the product: Rotating Residential or Rotating Mobile take a country, state, city, ZIP and ASN; Rotating Datacenter takes a country only; Static Residential takes no location. How many 1 with Different IP each time adds one rotating proxy; more adds that many sticky proxies, up to 1000 per pull, each holding its IP until ProxyEmpire's device goes offline, or for the Keep same IP time (up to 2 hours). HTTP or SOCKS5 on the same host and port. ProxyEmpire blocks payment, banking, crypto, AI, gaming, streaming and government sites by default.
geoHints.mountproxies: MountProxies sells dedicated 4G and 5G mobile proxies in the US, one modem per proxy, so a pull adds the proxies already on your account. Paste the API key from your MountProxies account page and leave How many blank to add them all. Each proxy is HTTP on its own port, with the username and password set in the MountProxies dashboard; proxies that use IP authorization only are left out. The city and carrier come with the modem. Rotate IP asks MountProxies for a new IP with the API key you saved here; it takes about 10 seconds.
geoHints.massive: Massive builds every proxy on its gateway, network.joinmassive.com: HTTP on port 65534, SOCKS5 on 65533. Enter the proxy username from your Massive dashboard (Profile) and your Massive API token as the password. Pick Residential (or mobile devices only) and a country; a state, city, ZIP code or ASN narrow it. How many 1 with no session adds one rotating proxy; more adds that many sticky proxies, up to 1000, each holding its IP for the Keep same IP time (15 minutes if blank, up to 24 hours). ISP proxies are US only, on isp.joinmassive.com:8000, with no location to pick. Massive blocks banking, gambling, adult and streaming sites.
geoHints.iproxy: iProxy.online turns your own Android phone and SIM into a mobile proxy, so a pull adds the proxy accesses already set up on your phones. Paste the user API key from the iProxy dashboard (making a new key stops the old one) and choose HTTP or SOCKS5; each proxy access is one of the two. Only accesses with a username and password are added. Each proxy keeps its phone's change-IP link, so Rotate IP gives the phone a new IP within seconds; all proxies on one phone change together. A phone without a change-IP link is added without one.
geoHints.weproxy: WEPROXY has no customer API, so the app builds the login on its gateway, gw.weproxy.com.tr:8989, which carries HTTP and SOCKS5 on the same port. Enter the proxy username and password from the WEPROXY panel (not your login email), then pick a country and, if you need one, a city. Each pull adds one rotating proxy with a new IP on every request. Sticky IPs are not available in the app yet. Traffic comes out of your WEPROXY pack, which does not expire until it is used.
geoHints.coronium: Coronium sells dedicated mobile proxies, so the app lists what is already on your account. Paste your API key (Dashboard, Account, API Access) and choose HTTP or SOCKS5. How many caps the import (blank = all). Expired lines are skipped. The location is fixed by the line, so there is nothing to target. Rotate the IP from the Coronium dashboard; rotation links are not stored in the app.
geoHints.simplyproxies: Simply Proxies is UK mobile only. Enter the proxy username and password from your dashboard. Every proxy is SOCKS5 on proxy.simplyproxies.com:6890, and SOCKS5 sends the proxy password in clear text, as Simply Proxies' docs note, so it can be read on the network path. Pick a network (EE, O2, Vodafone or Three) or leave it on Any; if no device on that network is free, the connection is refused rather than moved to another network. How many at 1 with no session gives one proxy with a new IP on each request; above 1 gives that many sticky IPs. Keep same IP sets how long each holds, up to 12 hours (2 hours and extending with use if blank). Sticky sessions are capped at a third of your pool.
geoHints.gonzoproxy: GonzoProxy runs every pool on connect.gonzoproxy.app:10000, HTTP or SOCKS5 on the same port. Copy the login and password from Proxy Setup in your dashboard; the pool is whichever one that login belongs to. Pick a country (required). State is optional and takes the numeric region code from the dashboard login (the 443 in sd_443), not a name. City is optional and works on residential logins only: GonzoProxy's mobile pool has no cities, and the app cannot tell which pool a login belongs to, so leave City blank on a mobile login. With How many at 1, no session and Keep same IP blank you get one proxy with a new IP on every request; above 1 you get that many sticky IPs (up to 1000), each held for the Keep same IP time (72 hours if you leave it blank, as in the dashboard). A session name lets you choose their names. The IP can change earlier if the device behind it goes offline.
geoHints.twoextract: 2extract uses each proxy's own login: dashboard, My Proxies, Connection Details. Paste the username (2xt-customer-<id>-proxy-<name>) and its password. Everything runs on proxy.2extract.net:5555. Set Protocol to the protocol chosen for that proxy in Connection Helper: HTTPS (2extract's default, TLS to the gateway), HTTP or SOCKS5. Pick a country, and optionally a state, city or ZIP code. Or leave the country on Any and enter an ASN to use one network instead; an ASN cannot be combined with a location. With How many at 1 and no session you get one proxy with a new IP on every request; above 1 you get that many sticky IPs (up to 1000), held for the Keep same IP time (10 minutes if you leave it blank, up to 24 hours). Rotating IP on demand is not wired here; start a new session name for a new IP.
geoHints.froxy: Froxy: open your subscription (My Subscriptions, Manage) and copy the Login and Password from Login/Password Access. The Pool type follows the type word the pasted password starts with (wifi is Residential, mobile is Mobile, shared is Datacenter); each Froxy subscription has its own login, so use the Mobile subscription's login for Mobile. Choose a country and optionally a region or city. Each proxy gets its own port from 9000 upwards (up to 1000 ports, 9000 to 9999), and each port keeps its own exit IP until the IP rotation time set on the subscription in the Froxy dashboard (90 to 3600 seconds). A pull takes the next ports your pool does not hold yet for that login, so ask for no more proxies than your package has ports left; Froxy refuses the rest. Residential, Mobile and Datacenter subscriptions always authorize by IP whitelist: add this computer's IP in the Froxy dashboard first, or the proxies are refused.
geoHints.nodemaven: NodeMaven builds every proxy on gate.nodemaven.com (8080 HTTP, 1080 SOCKS5). Enter the proxy username and password from the dashboard, Proxy Setup (not the account API key). Pick Residential or Mobile, a country and optionally a state or city (a city needs its state; write names with their spaces, for example New York). Every proxy uses NodeMaven's default quality filter (medium) and IPv4 exits only. How many 1 with no session name and Keep same IP blank gives one rotating proxy (a new IP on every request); otherwise the pull mints that many sticky IPs (up to 1000), each held for the Keep same IP time, or as long as NodeMaven can (up to 24 hours) when that is blank.
geoHints.marsproxies: MarsProxies uses your API token (Dashboard, Settings, API; it unlocks after 1 GB of residential traffic) to generate a residential proxy list for your sub-user. Enter the token plus the sub-user username and password. For the password, enter only the part before the first underscore: a password copied from the proxy list carries the targeting after it. Pick a country and optionally a state or city. How many 1 with Keep same IP blank gives one rotating proxy (a new IP on every request); more than 1, or a Keep same IP time, gives that many sticky proxies, up to 1000 per pull, each held for the Keep same IP time (up to 7 days; 24 hours if blank) while its device stays online. Traffic comes out of that sub-user's balance. Residential only.
geoHints.proxidize: Proxidize uses your API token (app.proxidize.com, Settings, API Token). For a Per-Proxy plan, also enter its Per-Proxy username: the app imports that plan's ready modems, and How many caps the import (blank = all). Leave Country, State, City and Sticky session blank there, because the modems are fixed. For a Per-GB plan, leave the username empty and pick Mobile or Residential; the app uses your first access point and builds sticky proxies on pg.proxi.es (20000 HTTP, 20002 SOCKS5, following Protocol), so enter a host or another port only if Proxy Details shows one. Pick a country (Mobile is United States only), optionally a state or city written as in the dashboard without spaces, and How many (up to 1000). A sticky IP usually holds 1 to 3 hours on Residential and 1 to 4 hours on Mobile.
geoHints.liveproxies: Live Proxies builds every proxy on its Enterprise (B2B) gateway (b2b.liveproxies.io:7383, SOCKS5 on socks.liveproxies.io:1080). Enter the Username (for example LV00000) and Password shown under Proxy Information on the dashboard, and pick a country: every Live Proxies line needs one. How many 1 with no session gives one rotating residential proxy; more than 1 gives that many sticky proxies (up to 1000), each with its own session, which Live Proxies holds for up to 60 minutes on residential plans (30 on mobile plans). A sticky session is 1 to 8 digits: with How many 1 it is used as typed, and with more each proxy adds its number to it.
geoHints.ipfoxy: IPFoxy builds every proxy on its rotating residential gateway (gate-us.ipfoxy.io:58688 for the Americas). You can enter gate.ipfoxy.io, gate-sg.ipfoxy.io (Asia-Pacific) or gate-de.ipfoxy.io (Europe) as the gateway instead; every route reaches every exit country. Enter the proxy account and password from the dashboard; the app adds customer- if it is missing. Pick a country and optionally a state and city. How many above 1, or a Keep same IP time, mints sticky IPs, up to 1000 per pull; How many 1 with both blank gives one proxy with a new IP on every request. IPFoxy holds a sticky IP for 30 or 60 minutes, so Keep same IP offers those two (30 minutes if blank). HTTP and SOCKS5 share the same port.
geoHints.mangoproxy: MangoProxy uses your API key to generate ready proxy lines. Enter the key and, optionally, the proxy sub-account username (blank uses the first sub-account on your account). Pick Residential, Residential light, Datacenter or ISP, a country (Load all countries, under the country list, shows only the countries that pool can target) and, on Residential and ISP, optionally a state, city or ASN (an ASN needs a country). Residential light and Datacenter target a country only. Then HTTP or SOCKS5, and how many (up to 1000; the API makes 100 per call, so a bigger pull takes a few seconds). Keep same IP sets the sticky session time (up to 120 minutes).
geoHints.ipburger: IP Burger builds every proxy on its residential gateway (residential.ipb.cloud:7777, HTTP only: their residential network has no SOCKS5). Enter the proxy username from the dashboard, Proxy Users (it starts with customer-) and that proxy user's password, not your account login. Pick a country, and optionally one city or state to narrow it. How many 1 with Sticky session and Keep same IP blank gives one proxy with a new IP on every request; How many above 1, a session name or a Keep same IP time mints sticky IPs, and Keep same IP sets how long each holds (up to 30 minutes; 30 if blank). If your dashboard shows another host, enter it as the gateway.
geoHints.proxy302: Proxy302 buys ready proxies through its Open API (proxy302.com). Create an API key in the Proxy302 console (API keys page) and enter the key id and the key secret; these are not your login. Pick the line your traffic is on. Premium can target a country, a state and a city (state and city by their names, and a city needs its state), and keeps Proxy302's fixed session time, or gives a new IP on every request if Keep same IP is Different IP each time. Standard targets a country only, and gives Different IP each time (rotating) or a sticky IP for 10, 30, 60 or 120 minutes. Pick HTTP or SOCKS5 and how many to add, up to 1000 per pull. Each proxy is a separate API purchase drawn from your Proxy302 traffic, on the host and port Proxy302 returns for it, so a large pull takes a few minutes.
geoHints.proxybrazil: ProxyBrazil sells dedicated 4G mobile proxies in Brazil (Claro or TIM, set by ProxyBrazil), so a pull adds the proxies already on your account, one per modem. In the ProxyBrazil dashboard open Integrations, create a key and pick SoftGlaze as the app; the key starts with pb_live_ and is shown once. Choose HTTP or SOCKS5 and leave How many blank to add them all. Each proxy keeps its rotation link, so Rotate IP gives it a new IP; a change can take up to a minute, ports on the same modem change together, and an account can change IP 30 times in 15 minutes. Proxies whose data allowance is used up are not added.
geoHints.proxyudp: ProxyUDP sells mobile 4G and 5G ports, so a pull adds the ports already on your account. Copy the API token from the ProxyUDP dashboard (API Access) and paste it here, choose HTTP or SOCKS5, and leave How many blank to add them all; the app reads each port's login from ProxyUDP, one request per port. The location and carrier come with the plan you bought. Rotate IP asks ProxyUDP for a new IP with your saved token; a busy modem may need a short wait, and the carrier may give back the same IP. Expired ports are skipped.
geoHints.zokol: Zokol sells French mobile proxies on Orange, SFR, Bouygues or Free, so a pull adds the proxies already on your account. Create an API key in the Zokol dashboard (API keys) and paste it here, choose HTTP or SOCKS5 (both ports share one login), and leave How many blank to add them all. Dedicated proxies keep their rotation link, so Rotate IP gives them a new IP, with a short wait between changes; shared proxies change IP on Zokol's schedule only. The carrier, IP version and fingerprint are set in the Zokol dashboard. Expired proxies are skipped.
geoHints.resiprox: ResiProx uses an API token from your dashboard. Pick Residential or Mobile (each has its own traffic), then a country, or load the list; a state and a city narrow it. How many 1 adds one rotating proxy with a new IP on every request; more adds that many sticky proxies, up to 50 per pull, each generated by ResiProx's API and kept as long as ResiProx can hold it. Every proxy runs on go.resiprox.com:5000, HTTP or SOCKS5. A set time per IP (1 to 200 minutes) is chosen in the ResiProx dashboard, not here.
geoHints.simplynode: SimplyNode uses an API key (dashboard, profile Settings) and one of your sub-accounts (proxy profiles). Pick Residential Essential, Residential Core or Mobile to match the sub-account, or type its login; left empty, the app uses the first one with traffic left. Choose a country, or load the list for that pool; a state and a city narrow it. How many 1 with Different IP each time adds one rotating proxy; more adds that many sticky proxies, up to 50 per pull, each generated by SimplyNode's API. Keep same IP sets how long each sticky proxy keeps its IP, up to 60 minutes (30 when blank). HTTP or SOCKS5. Traffic comes out of the sub-account's balance.
